claims.quote: PCDH19 syndrome is a monogenic epilepsy related to the protein protocadherin-19 (PCDH19) gene,
which encodes for a protein important for brain development.
The protein also seems to regulate gamma-aminobutyric acid type A receptors (GABA(A)(R)).

claims.object_text: refractory epilepsy with seizures occurring in clusters
claims.quote: The disease presents with refractory epilepsy that is characterized by seizures occurring in clusters.
GABA(A)(R) dysfunction and expression cause decreased effective inhibitory currents predisposing patients to epilepsy.
BBB dysfunction allows the passage of methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA)-type glutamate receptor antibodies (abs-NR) through the BBB susceptible membrane.
The cellular interference hypothesis establishes that the mutant and non-mutant cells interfere with each other's communication within the same tissue.

claims.object_text: female susceptibility to PCDH19-related cellular interference
claims.quote: Women are more susceptible to being affected by this hypothesis as men only have one copy of the x gene and interference is mediated by this gene, meaning that it cannot occur in them.

claims.object_text: AKR1C3/AKR1C2 product deficiency leading to decreased allopregnanolone and diminished GABA(A)(R) regulation
claims.quote: Finally, downregulation and deficiency of the AKR1C3/AKR1C2 products lead to decreasing levels of allopregnanolone, which diminish the regulation of GABA(A)(R).
